scope: Historical evaluation of the retired equal-requester prior. These metrics do not evaluate the current 60-day exponential song-priority.json; the original model and results are preserved unchanged.
selectionMetric: User-specified equal-requester rule, not tuned to holdout; event hit rates remain unweighted.

requesterAdjustment.policy: Each person receives min(1, distinct active days / 5) total weight. Divide that weight among their songs in proportion to 30-day decayed requests. Unknown, random and ambiguous requests share a single 0.25-weight pool. No person-specific exception.
requesterAdjustment.identityPolicy: Prefer stable user IDs; uniquely mapped display-name aliases use that ID; otherwise fall back to normalized display name, or unknown if ambiguous.

deduplication.ignored: Queue snapshots, user-data synchronization, routing messages and playback-end messages are not new requests.

limitations: Single observer and their visited rooms; not global popularity.
Display-name fallback can split renamed users or merge identical names when stable IDs are unavailable.
Recency decay affects each person’s relative song preferences; qualified people retain equal total weight even if inactive.
Request events do not prove completed playback.
Only recognizable WannaDance song IDs are counted, not other worlds or arbitrary URLs.
Time-window deduplication can merge fast intentional repeats or retain unusually delayed duplicates.
No current catalog or byte-size validation; top-K hit rate is not a 20-GiB cache simulation.
October holdout is short. Unseen songs require a separate fallback.
Scores are a separate prior, not synthetic local request history.
